newsitem.title: GERMANY: No basic change in French position on pact - Kinkel.
newsitem.headline: No basic change in French position on pact - Kinkel.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Tuesday he perceived no basic change in France's new position on the stability pact intended to underpin European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"I can't see that there is a change in the basic position of the French," Kinkel told reporters at a reception. He was responding to France's call to delay a planned stability pact which is due to be ratified at a European Union summit in Amsterdam next week.

Kinkel said he did not think Paris would hinder plans for EMU, behind which Germany and France have been the driving force. "(Plans for) the stability pact remains, the euro will arrive and the stability pact will arrive," Kinkel said.
The minister said he understood perfectly well that France's new left-wing government, which has been in office just over a week, needed more time to reflect on the pact.
The pact was proposed by German Finance Minister Theo Waigel last December to quell Germans' fears of swapping the deutschemark for what could be a weaker currency.

But at a meeting of EU finance ministers in Luxembourg on Monday, French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said Paris needed time to study the stability pact -- which is designed to enforce fiscal restraint among EMU member states.
